title: ICU infections, stewardship and the immunocompromised
summary: Infections in the ICU: severe CAP, HAP/VAP, carbapenem-resistant Gram-negatives per ICMR, invasive fungal disease, TB and HIV, febrile neutropenia and TLS, and antibiotic PK/PD with stewardship - aligned with NCDC/ICMR National Treatment Guidelines 2025.

topics.title: Severe community-acquired pneumonia
topics.summary: Identify severe CAP (ATS/IDSA criteria), start the Indian national empirical regimen within 1 h, add hydrocortisone, and think of Indian tropical mimics.

definition.text: Severe CAP (ATS/IDSA 2019): 1 major criterion (septic shock needing vasopressors, or respiratory failure needing mechanical ventilation) or ≥ 3 minor criteria (RR ≥ 30, PaO2/FiO2 ≤ 250, multilobar infiltrates, confusion, BUN ≥ 20 mg/dL, WBC < 4,000/mm³, platelets < 100,000/mm³, temperature < 36 °C, hypotension needing aggressive fluids).

steps.title: Recognise and admit to ICU
steps.detail: Apply ATS/IDSA criteria; CURB-65 ≥ 3 also flags high risk.

steps.title: Samples before antibiotics
steps.detail: Two blood cultures, sputum/tracheal aspirate Gram stain and culture, urinary pneumococcal and Legionella antigens, influenza/SARS-CoV-2 PCR; consider sputum GeneXpert for TB and scrub typhus/leptospira/dengue tests in the Indian monsoon setting.

steps.title: Empirical antibiotics within 1 h
steps.detail: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily + azithromycin 500 mg daily (or doxycycline 100 mg BD). Pseudomonas risk (bronchiectasis, recent antibiotics/hospital, immunosuppression): piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h + azithromycin. Add MRSA cover (vancomycin or linezolid) for necrotising pneumonia or post-influenza.

steps.title: Influenza
steps.detail: Oseltamivir 75 mg BD when influenza is suspected in season, without waiting for PCR.

steps.title: Hydrocortisone
steps.detail: Severe CAP (ICU, high-flow/NIV/ventilation): hydrocortisone 200 mg/day for 4-8 days with taper (CAPE COD). Not in influenza pneumonia.

steps.title: Respiratory support
steps.detail: HFNC or NIV trial with close monitoring (ROX index); lung-protective ventilation if intubated.

steps.title: De-escalate and stop
steps.detail: Narrow to culture results; stop macrolide when atypicals excluded; total 5-7 days if clinically stable (longer for S. aureus, Pseudomonas, lung abscess, empyema). If not resolving in 2 weeks, exclude TB.

doseCards.dose: 200 mg/day for 4 days (8 if still severe), then taper
doseCards.dilution: 200 mg in 50 mL NS over 24 h = ~2 mL/h

tables.title: Empirical ICU CAP regimens (NCDC/ICMR 2025)
rows: Ceftriaxone 2 g OD + azithromycin 500 mg OD (or doxycycline 100 mg q12h)
Cefotaxime 2 g TDS or piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h + azithromycin/doxycycline
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h + azithromycin or doxycycline
Add vancomycin 25 mg/kg load then 15 mg/kg q8-12h
Teicoplanin or linezolid 600 mg BD (after TB excluded)

redFlags.text: Diabetic from coastal South/East India with severe pneumonia, abscesses or septic shock: consider melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei) - needs meropenem or ceftazidime.

pitfalls.text: Delaying antibiotics for imaging or sputum when the patient is in shock.
Using a fluoroquinolone empirically in India where TB is common: it can mask and select resistant TB.

pearls.text: Procalcitonin should not be used to decide whether to start antibiotics in severe CAP, but can support stopping.

nodes.text: Hydrocortisone (no influenza); oseltamivir if flu suspected
Review cultures at 48-72 h; total 5-7 days

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: S. pneumoniae remains the leading cause; H. influenzae, S. aureus, Gram-negative bacilli (Klebsiella), atypicals (Legionella, Mycoplasma) and respiratory viruses (influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV) follow. Severe disease reflects dysregulated host response with lung injury and sepsis.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ATS/IDSA 2019 defines severe CAP and empirical regimens [Metlay 2019].
- ERS/ESICM/ESCMID/ALAT 2023 suggest corticosteroids for severe CAP without shock and macrolides in combination [Martin-Loeches 2023].
- CAPE COD: hydrocortisone reduced 28-day mortality (6.2% vs 11.9%) in severe CAP [Dequin 2023].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Steroids in influenza or in patients already in septic shock; macrolide vs doxycycline for atypical cover.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- The NCDC/ICMR National Treatment Guidelines (v2.0, 2025) set ceftriaxone + azithromycin/doxycycline as first line for ICU CAP.
- Indian CAP mimics: TB, scrub typhus, leptospirosis (pulmonary haemorrhage), melioidosis, H1N1 influenza and dengue; ask about season, occupation and geography.

quiz.explanation: Major criteria: vasopressors or mechanical ventilation.

topics.title: Hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia
topics.summary: Diagnose VAP carefully, choose empirical therapy from the local ICU antibiogram, cover MRSA and resistant Gram-negatives when indicated, and stop at 7 days.

definition.text: HAP: pneumonia ≥ 48 h after admission, not incubating at admission. VAP: pneumonia > 48 h after intubation. Diagnosis: new or progressive infiltrate plus ≥ 2 of fever, purulent secretions, leucocytosis/leucopenia, worsening oxygenation.

steps.title: Confirm clinically and microbiologically
steps.detail: Chest imaging (CXR/lung ultrasound), endotracheal aspirate semi-quantitative culture (or BAL/mini-BAL), blood cultures. Exclude atelectasis, pulmonary oedema, ARDS, PE.

steps.title: Assess resistance risk
steps.detail: Prior IV antibiotics within 90 days, septic shock, ARDS before VAP, ≥ 5 days hospital stay before onset, acute RRT, known colonisation, local MDR prevalence (in most Indian ICUs: high).

steps.title: Empirical therapy
steps.detail: Per ICU antibiogram. Without recent BL-BLI/carbapenem exposure: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h (or cefoperazone-sulbactam 3 g q12h). Recent BL-BLI/carbapenem exposure: meropenem ± polymyxin B (or colistin). Add vancomycin/linezolid if MRSA risk or MRSA > 10-20% locally.

steps.title: Optimise dosing
steps.detail: Loading doses, extended infusion of beta-lactams, TDM for vancomycin/aminoglycosides; consider CRRT/ARC effects.

steps.title: De-escalate at 48-72 h
steps.detail: Narrow to culture results; stop MRSA cover if cultures/nasal PCR negative; stop if alternative diagnosis.

steps.title: Duration 7 days
steps.detail: 7 days for most HAP/VAP regardless of organism if clinically improving (ICMR CRO guidance 7-10 days).

doseCards.dose: 4.5 g q6h over 3-4 h (first dose over 30 min)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg normal renal function: 4.5 g at 00, 06, 12, 18 h, each over 3 h (33 mL/h)

doseCards.dose: 1 g q8h (2 g q8h over 3 h for high MIC)
Load 25 mg/kg, then 15 mg/kg q8-12h; AUC 400-600
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 1,750 mg load over ~2 h, then 1 g q12h; level before 4th dose

redFlags.text: VAP with septic shock in an ICU with high CRE/CRAB rates: empirical polymyxin-containing regimen per antibiogram until cultures return.

pitfalls.text: Treating tracheal colonisation (positive culture without clinical pneumonia) - especially Acinetobacter.
Nebulised antibiotics for CRAB pneumonia: not recommended by ICMR.

pearls.text: A negative good-quality tracheal aspirate (no organisms, few neutrophils) in a patient without new antibiotics strongly argues against VAP.

nodes.text: Recent BL-BLI or carbapenem exposure / CRO colonised?
Reconsider diagnosis; stop if cultures negative and improving

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Micro-aspiration of colonised oropharyngeal and gastric secretions past the cuff, biofilm on the endotracheal tube, and impaired mucociliary clearance lead to VAP; pathogens are predominantly Gram-negative (Klebsiella, Acinetobacter, Pseudomonas) in Indian ICUs.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- IDSA/ATS 2016: 7 days for HAP/VAP, antibiogram-based empirical therapy, de-escalation [Kalil 2016].
- ERS/ESICM 2017 international HAP/VAP guideline [Torres 2017].
- NCDC/ICMR 2025 and ICMR CRO guidance 2022 give Indian empirical and directed regimens [NCDC 2025; ICMR 2022].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Diagnosis by clinical vs quantitative cultures; ventilator-associated tracheobronchitis treatment; inhaled antibiotics.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- ICMR AMRSN surveillance shows high carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae and very high resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii in Indian ICUs; generating a unit antibiogram is essential.
- Cefoperazone-sulbactam is commonly used in India and is listed as a first-line VAP option in national guidelines.

topics.title: Carbapenem-resistant and MDR Gram-negative infections
topics.summary: Mechanism-directed therapy for CRE (NDM, OXA-48, KPC), CRAB and CRPA following ICMR 2022 and IDSA 2024, with polymyxin dosing and infection control.

definition.text: CRE = Enterobacterales resistant to any carbapenem. In India, NDM (metallo-beta-lactamase) and OXA-48-like carbapenemases predominate, often together. CRAB and CRPA are carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

steps.title: Infection or colonisation?
steps.detail: Treat only clinical infection; Acinetobacter and Stenotrophomonas in respiratory or wound samples are often colonisers.

steps.title: Ask the lab for mechanism
steps.detail: Request carbapenemase testing (phenotypic/PCR: NDM, OXA-48, KPC) and ceftazidime-avibactam + aztreonam synergy testing.

steps.title: NDM (± OXA-48) CRE
steps.detail: First choice: ceftazidime-avibactam 2.5 g q8h + aztreonam 2 g q8h, both over 3 h (after synergy shown). Alternatives: polymyxin + another active agent (tigecycline, aminoglycoside, IV fosfomycin) or high-dose meropenem if MIC < 16.

steps.title: OXA-48-like or KPC CRE
steps.detail: Ceftazidime-avibactam 2.5 g q8h over 3 h (if susceptible). Meropenem-vaborbactam or imipenem-relebactam also options for KPC where available.

steps.title: CRAB
steps.detail: High-dose sulbactam (6-9 g/day; e.g. ampicillin-sulbactam 9 g q8h over 4 h) as backbone plus a second active agent (polymyxin, minocycline 200 mg q12h, tigecycline) for moderate-severe infection.

steps.title: CRPA
steps.detail: Use any susceptible beta-lactam (ceftazidime, cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam); newer agents (ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam) per susceptibility; polymyxin-based combination only when nothing else works.

steps.title: Polymyxin rules
steps.detail: Always load. Polymyxin B for systemic infections (no renal adjustment); colistin for UTI (renal excretion as active drug). Avoid tigecycline monotherapy for bacteraemia/pneumonia.

steps.title: Source control and infection control
steps.detail: Remove lines, drain collections; contact precautions, cohorting, rectal surveillance per policy, hand hygiene.

doseCards.dose: 2.5 g q8h (+ aztreonam 2 g q8h over 3 h for MBL)
doseCards.verify: Renal adjustment for both agents; synergy test before use.

doseCards.dose: Load 2.5 mg/kg (25,000 units/kg), then 1.5 mg/kg (15,000 units/kg) q12h
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 17.5 lakh units (175 mg) load over 2 h, then 10.5 lakh units (105 mg) q12h; Indian vial 5 lakh units
doseCards.verify: ICMR fixed doses 15 lakh load then 7.5 lakh q12h; NCDC 15-20 lakh then 7.5-10 lakh.

doseCards.role: CRO UTI or when polymyxin B unavailable
doseCards.dose: 9 million units load, then 4.5 million units q12h
doseCards.verify: Adjust maintenance for CrCl and CRRT.

tables.title: Mechanism-directed therapy (ICMR 2022)
rows: Polymyxin + active agent; high-dose meropenem if MIC < 16

redFlags.text: Septic shock with known CRE colonisation: empirical regimen must cover CRE until cultures are back.

pitfalls.text: Using polymyxin B for UTI (low urinary concentration) or colistin without a loading dose.
Empirical ceftazidime-avibactam + aztreonam: national guidance reserves it for targeted therapy.

pearls.text: Give ceftazidime-avibactam and aztreonam simultaneously (Y-site) so the inhibitor protects aztreonam at the same time.

nodes.text: Susceptible beta-lactam; polymyxin combo if none

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Carbapenemases hydrolyse carbapenems: serine enzymes (KPC, OXA-48) are inhibited by avibactam; metallo-beta-lactamases (NDM, VIM) are not but cannot hydrolyse aztreonam - hence aztreonam plus avibactam (which protects aztreonam from co-produced ESBL/AmpC).
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ICMR 2022 CRO guidance: Indian mechanism-based options and doses [ICMR 2022].
- IDSA 2024 AMR guidance [Tamma 2024].
- International polymyxin consensus 2019: loading doses, polymyxin B preferred for systemic infection, colistin for UTI [Tsuji 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Combination vs monotherapy for CRE; cefiderocol in CRAB; sulbactam-durlobactam (not available in India).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- India is a global hotspot for NDM-producing Enterobacterales; ICMR AMRSN annual reports document high carbapenem resistance in K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii.
- Polymyxin B vials in India are labelled in units (5 lakh units = 50 mg). Newer agents (e.g. cefepime-enmetazobactam) are entering the Indian market; use per susceptibility and stewardship approval.

topics.title: Invasive fungal infections: candidaemia, C. auris, aspergillosis, mucormycosis
topics.summary: Echinocandin-first candidaemia bundle, C. auris precautions, voriconazole for aspergillosis and urgent liposomal amphotericin plus surgery for mucormycosis.

definition.text: Invasive candidiasis (candidaemia, deep-seated) is the commonest ICU fungal infection. Invasive aspergillosis occurs in neutropenia, transplant, steroids, influenza/COVID-19 and COPD. Mucormycosis (rhino-orbito-cerebral) is strongly linked to uncontrolled diabetes and steroids in India.

steps.title: Candidaemia bundle
steps.detail: Echinocandin first line; remove/replace CVC; repeat blood cultures daily until negative; dilated fundoscopy (in neutropenia after recovery); echocardiography if persistent; 14 days after first negative culture and symptom resolution.

steps.title: Step-down
steps.detail: Switch to fluconazole after 5-7 days if isolate susceptible, patient stable and repeat cultures negative.

steps.title: Candida auris
steps.detail: Fluconazole-resistant, spreads in ICUs: echinocandin, contact precautions, single room, chlorine/peracetic-acid environmental cleaning, inform infection control.

steps.title: Do not treat candiduria or respiratory Candida
steps.detail: Usually colonisation; treat candiduria only in neutropenia, urological procedures or symptomatic infection.

steps.title: Aspergillosis
steps.detail: CT chest, serum/BAL galactomannan; voriconazole 6 mg/kg q12h × 2 then 4 mg/kg q12h (TDM); isavuconazole or L-AmB alternatives.

steps.title: Mucormycosis
steps.detail: Emergency: L-AmB 5 mg/kg/day (10 mg/kg CNS), urgent surgical debridement (ENT/maxillofacial/neurosurgery), control glucose and acidosis, reduce steroids/immunosuppression; step-down posaconazole/isavuconazole.

doseCards.notes: Micafungin 100 mg daily needs no load.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 12 mg/kg ≈ 800 mg, then 6 mg/kg ≈ 400 mg
70 kg: 420 mg × 2, then 280 mg q12h; trough day 5

doseCards.dilution: Reconstitute 50 mg vials; dilute in 5% dextrose (not saline) to 0.2-2 mg/mL over 2 h

redFlags.text: Diabetic with facial pain/swelling, black nasal eschar, ptosis or vision loss: suspect rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis - same-day imaging, biopsy, L-AmB and surgery.

pitfalls.text: Starting fluconazole empirically for candidaemia in an Indian ICU where C. auris/C. glabrata are common.
Leaving the central line in place in candidaemia.

pearls.text: Beta-D-glucan has a high negative predictive value for invasive candidiasis and can support stopping empirical antifungals.

nodes.text: Daily blood cultures; fundoscopy; echo if persistent
Contact precautions, single room, environmental cleaning
Step down to fluconazole; 14 days from first negative culture
Continue echinocandin 14 days from first negative culture

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Candida gains access from colonised gut or skin through CVCs, abdominal surgery and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Moulds are inhaled; angioinvasion causes infarction and necrosis, especially in mucormycosis where acidosis and high iron availability (DKA) drive growth.
consultantNotes.evidence: - IDSA 2016 candidiasis guideline [Pappas 2016]. IDSA 2016 aspergillosis guideline [Patterson 2016]. ECMM/MSG 2019 global mucormycosis guideline [Cornely 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Empirical antifungals in non-neutropenic ICU patients (EMPIRICUS showed no benefit); antifungal prophylaxis in high-risk surgical patients.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- India has high rates of C. auris and C. tropicalis candidaemia; national guidelines recommend echinocandins first line.
- India had the world's largest COVID-19-associated mucormycosis outbreak (2021); uncontrolled diabetes and steroid overuse remain key risk factors.
- Generic L-AmB is available but expensive; conventional amphotericin is cheaper but more nephrotoxic.

topics.title: Tuberculosis and HIV in the ICU
topics.summary: Start NTEP weight-band ATT for critically ill TB, steroids for TB meningitis, and manage PJP, cryptococcal meningitis and ART timing in advanced HIV.

definition.text: TB presents to the ICU as miliary TB with ARDS, TB meningitis, massive haemoptysis, TB-IRIS or drug-induced liver injury. In advanced HIV (CD4 < 200), PJP, cryptococcal meningitis, TB and bacterial sepsis dominate.

steps.title: Diagnose TB quickly
steps.detail: Sputum/tracheal aspirate/BAL GeneXpert (CBNAAT/TrueNat) with rifampicin resistance, CSF Xpert Ultra and ADA, urine LAM in HIV, imaging; start empirical ATT if high suspicion and critically ill.

steps.title: ATT
steps.detail: 2HRZE/4HRE by NTEP weight band (extend continuation to 10 months for CNS TB). Give by NG if needed; IV options limited.

steps.title: TB meningitis steroids
steps.detail: Dexamethasone 0.4 mg/kg/day IV in divided doses during admission, tapered over 6-8 weeks (HIV-negative).

steps.title: Drug-induced liver injury
steps.detail: Stop hepatotoxic drugs if ALT > 3× with symptoms or > 5× without, or bilirubin rise; give non-hepatotoxic bridge (e.g. ethambutol + levofloxacin + streptomycin/linezolid per specialist); reintroduce sequentially.

steps.title: PJP
steps.detail: CD4 < 200, hypoxaemia, bilateral ground-glass: cotrimoxazole 15-20 mg/kg/day (TMP) in 3-4 doses × 21 days + prednisolone if PaO2 < 70 mmHg.

steps.title: Cryptococcal meningitis
steps.detail: Single L-AmB 10 mg/kg + 14 days flucytosine 100 mg/kg/day + fluconazole 1,200 mg/day (WHO 2022); therapeutic LPs for raised opening pressure (> 25 cm H2O).

steps.title: ART timing
steps.detail: Continue ART if already on it. New diagnosis: start within 2 weeks for most OIs (including PJP, and TB if CD4 < 50); delay 4-6 weeks in cryptococcal meningitis and TB meningitis (IRIS risk).

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 5 tablets of HRZE (75/150/400/275) daily for 8 weeks
70 kg: 28 mg/day (e.g. 8 mg q8h ≈ 24 mg or 7 mg q6h)
70 kg: TMP 1,050-1,400 mg/day, e.g. 2 double-strength (160/800 mg) tablets q6h = TMP 1,280 mg/day

doseCards.dose: 40 mg BD × 5 days, 40 mg OD × 5 days, 20 mg OD × 11 days

redFlags.text: TB meningitis with falling GCS: hydrocephalus - urgent CT and neurosurgical review (VP shunt/EVD).

pitfalls.text: Empirical fluoroquinolone or linezolid for 'pneumonia' masking TB.
Starting ART immediately in cryptococcal meningitis: increased mortality from IRIS.

pearls.text: Rifampicin markedly lowers levels of azoles, many ART drugs, steroids and warfarin - review all drug interactions on starting ATT.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Miliary TB causes diffuse granulomatous lung injury and ARDS; TB meningitis causes basal exudates, vasculitis, infarcts and hydrocephalus. HIV-related CD4 depletion predisposes to opportunistic infections; ART-driven immune recovery can cause IRIS.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Thwaites 2004: dexamethasone reduced mortality in TB meningitis (RR 0.69) in HIV-negative adults [Thwaites 2004].
- WHO 2022: single high-dose L-AmB induction for cryptococcal meningitis [WHO 2022].
- NIH OI guidelines: cotrimoxazole + adjunctive steroids for PJP [NIH OI].
consultantNotes.controversies: - High-dose rifampicin for TB meningitis; outcomes of mechanical ventilation in TB-ARDS.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- India has the world's highest TB burden; notify all TB cases on Ni-kshay and link to NTEP (free drugs, nutritional support).
- NACO provides free ART; ART centres guide regimens (dolutegravir-based first line); check rifampicin-dolutegravir interaction (dolutegravir twice daily).

topics.title: Febrile neutropenia and tumour lysis syndrome
topics.summary: Antipseudomonal beta-lactam within 1 h for febrile neutropenia, escalation rules, and prevention/treatment of TLS with fluids, rasburicase and early RRT.

definition.text: Febrile neutropenia: ANC < 500/mm³ (or expected to fall below 500 within 48 h) with single temperature ≥ 38.3 °C or ≥ 38.0 °C sustained for 1 h. TLS (Cairo-Bishop): ≥ 2 of uric acid ≥ 8 mg/dL, K ≥ 6 mmol/L, phosphate ≥ 4.5 mg/dL, Ca ≤ 7 mg/dL within 3 days before to 7 days after therapy; clinical TLS adds AKI, arrhythmia or seizures.

steps.title: FN: antibiotics within 1 h
steps.detail: Cultures (peripheral + each lumen), then piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h (or cefoperazone-sulbactam). Unstable: meropenem 1 g q8h + vancomycin ± polymyxin B (per NCDC 2025 and CRO risk).

steps.title: When to add vancomycin
steps.detail: Haemodynamic instability, pneumonia, suspected line infection, skin/soft tissue infection, MRSA colonisation, Gram-positive bacteraemia pending ID; stop at 48 h if no Gram-positive infection.

steps.title: Antifungal
steps.detail: If febrile after 72-96 h with negative cultures and unstable: CT chest, galactomannan/beta-D-glucan, and echinocandin or mould-active agent.

steps.title: De-escalate/stop
steps.detail: Stop if afebrile for 3 days and cultures negative, with close observation, even before count recovery (ECIL-4 / NCDC).

steps.title: TLS prevention
steps.detail: Risk-stratify (bulky lymphoma, ALL/AML with high WBC, high LDH, CKD). IV fluids 2-3 L/m²/day aiming urine output 80-100 mL/m²/h; allopurinol (intermediate risk); rasburicase (high risk). Avoid urinary alkalinisation.

steps.title: Established TLS
steps.detail: Rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg; treat hyperkalaemia; do not treat asymptomatic hypocalcaemia (calcium-phosphate precipitation); early RRT for refractory hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, fluid overload or oliguria.

doseCards.role: FN where local ESBL rates low

doseCards.dose: 0.2 mg/kg over 30 min daily (up to 5 days)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 14 mg; many units use a single 3-6 mg dose and repeat by uric acid
BSA 1.8 m²: 180 mg q8h (e.g. 200 mg q8h)

tables.title: Cairo-Bishop laboratory TLS (≥ 2 within 3 days before to 7 days after therapy)
tables.caption: Clinical TLS = laboratory TLS + creatinine ≥ 1.5 × ULN, arrhythmia/sudden death, or seizure.

redFlags.text: Neutropenic patient with hypotension: septic shock until proven otherwise - antibiotics before any imaging.

pitfalls.text: Rasburicase in G6PD deficiency: severe haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia.
Giving calcium for asymptomatic hypocalcaemia in TLS with high phosphate.

pearls.text: Rasburicase continues to degrade uric acid in the blood tube: send samples on ice for accurate levels.

nodes.text: Afebrile 3 days, cultures negative: stop or de-escalate

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Neutropenia removes the main defence against bacteria and fungi; mucositis and lines permit translocation. TLS results from rapid tumour cell lysis releasing potassium, phosphate and nucleic acids (metabolised to uric acid), causing crystal nephropathy, arrhythmias and calcium-phosphate deposition.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- IDSA 2010 FN guideline [Freifeld 2011]; NCDC/ICMR 2025 Indian FN regimens [NCDC 2025].
- TLS evidence-based review [Coiffier 2008]; Cairo-Bishop classification [Cairo 2004].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Early stopping of antibiotics before neutrophil recovery; prophylactic fluoroquinolones in high MDR settings.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- High rates of ESBL and carbapenem resistance in Indian oncology units mean NCDC suggests meropenem + vancomycin ± polymyxin B for unstable FN.
- G6PD deficiency is common in several Indian communities; test before rasburicase.

topics.title: Antibiotic PK/PD, TDM, procalcitonin and stewardship
topics.summary: Dose antibiotics for critical illness (loading, extended infusion, AUC-guided vancomycin), use procalcitonin to stop, and keep courses short.

definition.text: Beta-lactams are time-dependent (target fT > MIC), aminoglycosides concentration-dependent (Cmax/MIC 8-10), and vancomycin AUC-dependent (AUC/MIC 400-600). Critical illness alters volume of distribution and clearance (augmented renal clearance, AKI, CRRT, hypoalbuminaemia).

steps.title: Load fully
steps.detail: Give full loading doses regardless of renal function (Vd is increased in sepsis); adjust only maintenance doses.

steps.title: Prolonged beta-lactam infusion
steps.detail: After a 30-min loading dose, give piperacillin-tazobactam, meropenem, cefepime as extended (3-4 h) or continuous infusion; meta-analysis showed lower 90-day mortality.

steps.title: Aminoglycosides once daily
steps.detail: Amikacin 15-25 mg/kg or gentamicin 5-7 mg/kg once daily (if used); trough monitoring.

steps.title: Vancomycin AUC dosing
steps.detail: Load 20-35 mg/kg; AUC 400-600 mg·h/L by two levels or Bayesian software; trough 15-20 as surrogate where AUC not feasible.

steps.title: Procalcitonin to stop
steps.detail: Stop antibiotics when PCT < 0.5 ng/mL or falls ≥ 80% from peak, if clinically improving (not to start antibiotics in shock).

steps.title: Short courses
steps.detail: CAP 5-7 days; HAP/VAP 7; intra-abdominal infection with source control 4 days (STOP-IT); uncomplicated Gram-negative bacteraemia 7 days (BALANCE).

steps.title: Stewardship time-out at 48-72 h
steps.detail: Review cultures, de-escalate, IV-to-oral switch, document indication and stop date; unit antibiogram every 6-12 months.

doseCards.dose: 1 g q8h over 3 h after 30-min first dose
doseCards.verify: Meropenem stability at room temperature in Indian ICUs (~8 h at 25 °C; less at higher temperatures).

redFlags.text: Young trauma/sepsis patient with high urine output and low creatinine (CrCl > 130 mL/min): augmented renal clearance - standard doses may be subtherapeutic.

pitfalls.text: Halving the first dose of a beta-lactam because of AKI.
Continuing 'just to complete 14 days' when the evidence supports shorter courses.

pearls.text: Write the stop date when you start an antibiotic.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Capillary leak and fluid resuscitation increase Vd of hydrophilic drugs (beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, vancomycin); hyperdynamic circulation increases renal clearance; hypoalbuminaemia increases free fraction and clearance of highly bound drugs.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Abdul-Aziz 2024 meta-analysis (18 RCTs): prolonged beta-lactam infusion reduced 90-day mortality; BLING III showed a non-significant reduction [Abdul-Aziz 2024; Dulhunty 2024].
- SAPS: PCT guidance reduced antibiotic duration and mortality [de Jong 2016].
- STOP-IT: 4 days after source control as good as longer [Sawyer 2015]. BALANCE: 7 days non-inferior to 14 days for bacteraemia [BALANCE 2025].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Routine beta-lactam TDM; PCT cost-effectiveness in India.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- India's Kerala AMR strategy and ICMR AMSP programme promote stewardship; Schedule H1 restricts sale of many antibiotics.
- PCT and TDM are available mainly in larger centres; in their absence, use clinical response and short fixed durations.

quiz.stem: Loading dose of vancomycin in AKI:

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.adultDose: 2 g IV once daily for 5-7 days.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.adultDose: 500 mg IV/oral once daily for 3-5 days.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone
drugs.adultDose: Severe CAP: 200 mg/day IV (infusion) for 4 days, extended to 8 days if still severe, then taper (total 8 or 14 days).
drugs.cautions: Not studied in influenza pneumonia or septic shock at enrolment in CAPE COD; hyperglycaemia.

drugs.name: Oseltamivir
drugs.indications: Suspected/confirmed influenza (including H1N1) in severe CAP
drugs.adultDose: 75 mg orally/NG twice daily for 5 days (longer if still shedding/severe).

drugs.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
drugs.indications: HAP/VAP, febrile neutropenia, CAP with Pseudomonas risk
drugs.adultDose: 4.5 g IV q6h; extended infusion over 3-4 h (or continuous after loading) in critically ill.

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.indications: ESBL infection; HAP/VAP after BL-BLI exposure; febrile neutropenia with instability
drugs.adultDose: 1 g IV q8h (2 g q8h over 3 h for high-MIC organisms, CNS infection or CRE with MIC < 16 per ICMR).

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.indications: MRSA cover (pneumonia, line infection, febrile neutropenia with instability)
drugs.adultDose: Load 20-35 mg/kg (actual weight, max 3 g), then 15-20 mg/kg q8-12h; AUC-guided 400-600 mg·h/L (trough 15-20 mg/L as surrogate if AUC not available).
drugs.renalHepatic: Dose by levels; extend interval in AKI.

drugs.name: Linezolid
drugs.adultDose: 600 mg IV/oral q12h.
drugs.cautions: Thrombocytopenia after 10-14 days; serotonin syndrome; avoid as empirical in possible TB (ICMR).

drugs.name: Ceftazidime-avibactam (± aztreonam)
drugs.indications: KPC/OXA-48 CRE (alone); NDM (MBL) CRE with aztreonam after synergy testing
drugs.adultDose: 2.5 g IV q8h over 3 h; for MBL: plus aztreonam 2 g IV q8h over 3 h given simultaneously.
drugs.cautions: Reserve agent; not for empirical use per national guidelines.

drugs.name: Polymyxin B
drugs.indications: CRE, CRAB, CRPA when no better agent (not for UTI)
drugs.adultDose: Loading 2.5 mg/kg (25,000 units/kg) over 2 h, then 1.5 mg/kg (15,000 units/kg) q12h; Indian guidance: 15-20 lakh units load, then 7.5-10 lakh units q12h.
drugs.cautions: Nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, skin pigmentation; use in combination for severe infections.

drugs.name: Colistin (colistimethate sodium)
drugs.indications: CRE/CRAB infections, preferred polymyxin for UTI
drugs.adultDose: 9 million units IV loading, then 4.5 million units q12h (normal renal function).
drugs.renalHepatic: Reduce maintenance by CrCl; supplement on CRRT.

drugs.name: Ampicillin-sulbactam (high dose)
drugs.adultDose: 9 g (6 g ampicillin + 3 g sulbactam) IV q8h over 4 h (sulbactam 9 g/day), usually with a second active agent.

drugs.name: Caspofungin (or micafungin/anidulafungin)
drugs.adultDose: Caspofungin 70 mg IV load, then 50 mg daily; micafungin 100 mg daily; anidulafungin 200 mg load, then 100 mg daily.

drugs.name: Fluconazole
drugs.adultDose: 800 mg (12 mg/kg) load, then 400 mg (6 mg/kg) daily.
drugs.renalHepatic: Halve maintenance if CrCl < 50 (not on RRT).
drugs.cautions: C. auris, C. krusei and many C. glabrata are resistant.

drugs.name: Voriconazole
drugs.adultDose: 6 mg/kg IV q12h × 2 doses, then 4 mg/kg q12h; TDM trough 1-5.5 mg/L.
drugs.cautions: Many interactions, visual disturbance, hepatotoxicity; IV vehicle accumulates if CrCl < 50 (use oral).

drugs.name: Liposomal amphotericin B
drugs.adultDose: Mucormycosis 5 mg/kg/day (10 mg/kg/day for CNS); candidiasis 3-5 mg/kg/day; cryptococcal meningitis single 10 mg/kg (WHO 2022).
drugs.cautions: Hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, nephrotoxicity (less than conventional); pre-hydrate with saline.

drugs.name: HRZE fixed-dose combination (NTEP)
drugs.indications: Drug-sensitive TB including miliary and TB meningitis
drugs.adultDose: Daily FDC (H 75/R 150/Z 400/E 275 mg) by weight band: 35-49 kg 3 tablets, 50-64 kg 4, 65-75 kg 5, > 75 kg 6. Equivalent H 5, R 10, Z 25, E 15 mg/kg.
drugs.cautions: Hepatotoxicity (check LFT), rifampicin interactions (azoles, ART, warfarin); add pyridoxine 10 mg/day.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.adultDose: 0.4 mg/kg/day IV in divided doses, tapered over 6-8 weeks.

drugs.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
drugs.adultDose: 15-20 mg/kg/day of trimethoprim component IV/oral in 3-4 divided doses for 21 days.
drugs.cautions: Hyperkalaemia, marrow suppression, rash/SJS, AKI; G6PD.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.indications: Moderate-severe PJP (PaO2 < 70 mmHg or A-a gradient ≥ 35)
drugs.adultDose: 40 mg BD days 1-5, 40 mg daily days 6-10, 20 mg daily days 11-21 (start within 72 h of PJP therapy).

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.adultDose: 2 g IV q8h (extended infusion in critically ill).

drugs.name: Rasburicase
drugs.indications: Established TLS or high risk of TLS
drugs.adultDose: 0.2 mg/kg IV over 30 min daily for up to 5 days (single fixed 3-6 mg doses often effective).
drugs.cautions: Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (haemolysis, methaemoglobinaemia); sample for uric acid on ice.

drugs.name: Allopurinol
drugs.adultDose: 100 mg/m² q8h orally (max 800 mg/day), starting 1-2 days before chemotherapy.
